text.p: The Australian Gas Light Co (AGL) said on Friday it has restructured its management to reflect the move towards national open-access energy markets.
The company's major business functions will be organised into an energy infrastructure group and an energy sales and marketing group, managing director Len Bleasel said.

The changes are part of the move to a gas market where third parties can buy and transport gas through AGL's pipeline system, and the eventual establishment of a multi-access national energy market, AGL said.
They also included ring-fencing arrangements to separate the company's functions as required by recent regulations for the deregulation of the New South Wales gas market.

Bleasel said the infrastructure group under Greg Martin, formerly general manager energy utilities, would be responsible for the construction, operation, maintenance and utilisation of all AGL's gas pipelines and gas distribution networks.

Sales and marketing functions, including energy contracts and trading, would be included with energy services and market product development under Michael Fraser, formerly general manager wholesale energy.
